target: backend at http://127.0.0.1:8001 (uvicorn, trained models, PostgreSQL 17 seeded with 60 demo bugs)
scope: all 46 paths / 59 operations imported from docs/openapi.json (57 URLs), passive and active scan with the default policy, signed in as the seeded Administrator through a bearer token added to every request
excluded: /api/v1/auth/logout and /api/v1/users/me/password (would end the scan's own session)

alerts.name: Cross Site Scripting Weakness (Persistent in JSON Response)
alerts.verdict: Not a vulnerability in this design
alerts.reason: The API stores text exactly as submitted and returns it as application/json with X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and Cache-Control: no-store, so a browser never renders it as HTML. The only client, the VS Code webview, inserts server text as text nodes under a nonce-based Content Security Policy; tests check that markup in titles is stored and shown inertly.

alerts.name: Timestamp Disclosure - Unix
alerts.reason: The number is the version tag of the duplicate-detection model, a training timestamp, not a secret.

alerts.name: Authentication Request Identified
alerts.reason: ZAP identifying the login request; no finding.

alerts.name: User Agent Fuzzer
alerts.reason: ZAP's user-agent fuzzer saw no difference in behaviour; no finding.

found_by_review_of_the_scan_responses.issue: GET /api/v1/ai/status returned the severity model's training-set path on the server (for example ..\data\raw\zenodo_eclipse) to any signed-in user
found_by_review_of_the_scan_responses.fix: app/ai/engine.py public_meta() now returns only the dataset name; test_ai_status_names_the_dataset_without_its_server_path

not_covered: The VS Code webview itself (not a web page ZAP can crawl), TLS (checked separately, tls_check.json), denial of service, and business-logic flaws beyond the authorisation tests in backend/tests.
